sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Quantitative immunoblotting in Sf9 cell membranes: FLAG-tagged NTF detected by FLAG M1 antibody; GPS autoproteolytic cleavage confirmed at wild-type efficiency.
sites.rationale: GPR114 is the gene product of ADGRG5; the paper's construct is the same protein. The HA signal peptide replaces the native signal peptide (residues 1–21), placing the FLAG epitope at the mature extracellular N-terminus, which begins at residue 22 (E). No specific residue number is stated in the paper, so the junction is topology-derived: insert_after_residue=21 is the only possible extracellular N-terminal position. Python confirmed residue 21 = T and residue 22 = E, and the mature N-terminus is 228 residues from the first TM helix, providing ample space for a short tag. Full-length GPR114 (ADGRG5) constructs were engineered with an exogenous N-terminal hemagglutinin signal peptide followed by a FLAG epitope and a TEV protease site, expressed in Sf9 cells. L3 confirms the FLAG-tagged N-terminal fragment (NTF) was detected by anti-FLAG M1 immunoblotting and that GPS autoproteolytic cleavage was preserved.

sources.claim: All constructs examining cleavage efficiencies included an N-terminal hemagglutinin signal peptide followed by a FLAG epitope and a tobacco etch virus proteolytic site.

literature_notes: L2 and L3 together describe a C-terminal GFP-His8 tag on full-length GPR114. The topology landmarks place residues 506–528 in the intracellular compartment, so this tag is cytoplasmic and does not qualify as a surface tag site; it is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line grounds any internal extracellular loop insertion for ADGRG5 or a close ortholog, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GFP-His8 tag on full-length GPR114; the C-terminus (residues 506–528) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the cell surface.
